intro: Nearby examples can disagree. Make the distance ordering and voting tie rules explicit before trusting a nearest-neighbor prediction.
task: Return one predicted integer label per query using unweighted k-nearest-neighbor classification.
requirements: train and queries are nonempty finite matrices with matching positive feature counts. labels has one nonnegative integer value per training row.
k is an integer from 1 through the number of training rows, excluding booleans.
Rank by squared distance, breaking distance ties by original training index. Vote among k neighbors; class ties select the smallest label. Return a NumPy vector.
Do not modify inputs. Raise ValueError for the invalid shapes, ranges, or non-finite numeric inputs described above. Numerical checks use moderate finite values unless stated otherwise.

hints.title: Choose the representation
hints.body: Compute one distance per training row for each query, then use a stable sort.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: Count labels only after selecting neighbors. The closest individual label does not always win.

explanation: Nearest-neighbor classification stores examples instead of fitting a coefficient vector. The metric and feature scale become part of the model.
Neighbor selection and class voting have separate ties. Stable distance ordering determines membership at the cutoff, then the smallest class wins a tied vote.
Change k for a query near a class boundary. Explain why increasing the neighborhood can reduce sensitivity to a single example while also hiding local structure.
formula: prediction(q) = majority label among k nearest rows
